ConocoPhillips fell 4.1% today as crude oil prices tumbled more than 7% on growing hopes for a U.S.-Iran diplomatic deal. Oil is the primary driver of an oil major's profits—when crude prices drop sharply, so do earnings expectations. The decline came despite the stock hitting a recent high of $154 just two trading days earlier, signaling that the sudden pivot toward peace talks overrode any near-term momentum.

The broader context here is geopolitical risk pricing. Weeks of Middle East tensions had kept oil elevated; news of active U.S.-Iran diplomacy and Qatari mediation efforts shifted that calculation overnight, with traders betting on reduced supply disruption risk and therefore lower oil demand going forward. This type of headline-driven reversal is typical when military escalation fears ease.
